alex_support: FYI customer on Dedicated (us-east) hit a nasty streaming regression. After token rotation their client reconnects and gets a partial response duplicated + they were billed for both partials. Repro steps below.
maria_engineer: Ugh. Any logs or a minimal repro? Is this SSE or the SDK iterator?

alex_support: SSE via our Python SDK but reproducible with raw curl. Short logs show truncated final chunk, client reconnects, server resumes and re-emits overlapping prefix. Billing team saw two token bills for overlapping tokens.

alex_support: Repro (python async) — simplified:

```python
import asyncio
import httpx

async def stream_once(token):
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Accept": "text/event-stream"}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=None) as c:
        async with c.stream("GET", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate", headers=headers) as r:
            async for line in r.aiter_lines():
                if not line.strip():
                    continue
                print(line)

async def test():
    t1 = "TOKEN_A"
    task = asyncio.create_task(stream_once(t1))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.9)  # simulate mid-response cancel
    task.cancel()
    # rotate token and reconnect quickly
    t2 = "TOKEN_B"
    await stream_once(t2)

asyncio.run(test())
```

alex_support: Curl version that shows the SSE frames (sequence):

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate

# server emits:
# data: {"delta":"Hel"}

# connection closes (truncated)
# client reconnects with rotated token
# server emits:
# data: {"delta":"Hel"}
# data: {"delta":"lo"}

# result: client sees Hel, then Hello (duplicate "Hel")
```

maria_engineer: That duplicate/overlap suggests the server resumed from a prefix but the client also repros the prefix locally (iterator state). Two fast reconnects + auth rotation race. Do we have idempotency/sequence IDs in frames?

alex_support: No sequence id in this stream type. Customer was using default SDK iterator (async) without any resume token handling.

ryan_eng: Possible root cause: resume handshake relies on last-ack timestamp, but when token rotates we spawn a new connection without telling router to drop cached prefix. Combined with SDK re-sending buffered prefix we end up with duplicate tokens counted in billing. I can reproduce locally with a tight cancel/reconnect like yours.

sam_support: Customer got billed twice for overlapping tokens — they noticed two billing entries: one for the partial (200 tokens) and another for resumed tokens (180 overlapping). Can we credit? Also we need immediate mitigation.

elaine_sre: For mitigation: 1) Disable auto-reconnect on client while token rotation occurs, or 2) ensure new connection includes X-Resume-From: <last_event_id> header so server can drop overlapping frames. Billing: we can issue a one-time credit if duplicate token range overlaps; billing needs the two request IDs.

alex_support: For immediate reproability, here's the server-side trace we captured (trimmed):

"[2026-03-01T15:02:18.512Z] connection 0xabc: client close during frame 45 (prefix bytes 3)"
"[2026-03-01T15:02:18.614Z] token rotate for tenant 123, new token issued"
"[2026-03-01T15:02:18.616Z] connection 0xdef: resume requested, no last_event_id provided, resume defaults to prefix-replay"

ryan_eng: I'm going to push a small agent-side guard: if reconnect happens within 1s of token rotation, server will mark resume = strict and drop frames until ack. Pushing to staging now.
deploy-bot: rolled out staging patch redwood/stream-resume-guard@staging (sha: f7a1c2) to us-east/staging

maria_engineer: Good. Longer term: SDKs should expose a resume policy and include frame-level ids. I'll add a TODO to model-onboarding backlog: stream frames should include monotonic chunk_id and optional client-ack header.

sam_support: For customer comms: request both request-id headers (X-Req-Id) from their logs + timestamps so billing can reconcile. I'll draft the credit once we confirm overlap.

alex_support: Customer applied staging patch and verified that the duplicated prefix stopped when they set a 250ms reconnect delay after cancel. They still want a fix that doesn't require manual delay.

elaine_sre: Action items: (1) engine: keep resume-strict guard for <2s after token rotation, (2) SDK: add resume_policy with "drop_prefix" and expose graceful backoff hooks, (3) billing: add dedupe window for partial stream tokens.

ryan_eng: I'll open a PR with the server guard + tests to prevent replayed prefixes. Also adding a regression test that simulates cancel+rotate+reconnect.

maria_engineer: I'll prototype frame ids in the JS and Python SDKs and a tiny migration in staging. We'll flag this for a hotfix release.

sam_support: Thanks — I'll notify the customer and ask for the two X-Req-Id values. Quick question: any chance this also affects websockets?

ryan_eng: Possibly — same resume logic used by both transports. We'll extend tests.

alex_support: Ok, closing loop here: customers want credits + fix. I'll escalate billing request and send the repro to eng. Thanks all :thumbsup:
